site.name: Museum of Isfahan: The Safavid Court
site.concept: A scholarly museum dedicated to the arts, architecture, and courtly life of Safavid Iran (1501–1736).

card_pattern: Each content card sits on a deep cobalt surface framed by a thin gold filet, with a small palmette ornament at upper-left and a turquoise rule beneath the card title. Object cards are square-ish, roughly 1:1.1, with a centered ogee-arch image well, gold caption text in small caps, and ivory body text. Cards are arranged in symmetric grids of two or three across, never asymmetrically staggered.
design_rules: The site reads as cobalt-and-gold tilework: dense ornament concentrated at borders and around openings, with calm cream-on-cobalt fields between. Symmetry is non-negotiable — every major block is centered on a vertical axis, and ornament mirrors left-to-right. Display type is tight, gold, and inscriptional; body type is generously leaded ivory.

pages.title: Museum of Isfahan — The Safavid Court
pages.content_brief: Landing page introducing the museum as a center for Safavid studies, founded in 1971 in the Chahar Bagh district. Hero band features an ogee-arch frame over the words 'Beneath the Half of the World.' Below: three featured panels — a current exhibition on Riza Abbasi, a notice on the newly conserved Ardabil-style carpet fragment, and visiting hours. Closing band gives address and a quotation from Chardin's Voyages.

pages.title: Galleries & Permanent Collection
pages.content_brief: Overview of the permanent collection across seven galleries: Tilework of the Maydan, Manuscripts of the Royal Atelier, Silks and Velvets of Yazd, Metalwork and Inlaid Steel, Coinage of Shah Abbas I, Polychrome Mina'i and Lustreware, and the Reconstructed Iwan. Each gallery gets a square card with object count, era span, and a curator's name (e.g., Dr. Pardis Kermani, Curator of Manuscripts). Footer of the page lists recent acquisitions from 2023–2024.

pages.title: Current Exhibition — Riza Abbasi & the Isfahan Style
pages.content_brief: Featured exhibition page for 'Riza Abbasi and the Isfahan Style: Drawings from the Royal Library, 1598–1635,' running 14 March – 28 September 2024 in the Chehel Sotoun Gallery. Includes wall-text excerpt, a checklist of fourteen featured works (album leaves, single-figure studies, calligraphic sheets), loan credits from the Topkapı and the Reza Abbasi Museum, and a note on conservation by the Hossein Mirjafari Lab.

pages.title: Visit — Hours, Tickets & Directions
pages.content_brief: Practical visiting information. Address: 17 Chahar Bagh Abbasi Avenue, Isfahan. Hours: Tuesday–Sunday, 09:00–17:30; closed Mondays and Nowruz week. General admission 250,000 IRR; students and scholars 120,000; under 12 free. Audio guides available in Farsi, English, French, and German. Sections on accessibility (the Iwan Gallery is reached by a step-free ramp installed 2019), public transit (Metro Line 1, Si-o-Se Pol stop), and group bookings via the Education Office.

pages.title: Scholarship & The Royal Atelier Library
pages.content_brief: Page for visiting researchers. Describes the Royal Atelier Library of 22,000 volumes specializing in Safavid material culture, open by appointment to credentialed scholars. Lists current fellowships (the Shah Abbas Fellowship in Architectural History; the Mehrnaz Vossoughi Fellowship in Textile Conservation), the annual symposium ('Patterns of Patronage,' 6–8 November 2024), and recent monographs published by the museum press.

pages.title: About the Museum & Patronage
pages.content_brief: History of the museum: founded 1971 by the Pahlavi-era Society for National Monuments, reorganized 1983 under the Ministry of Cultural Heritage, expanded 2008 with the Maydan Wing designed by Nader Ardalan. Names the Director (Dr. Hossein Mirjafari), Chief Curator (Dr. Pardis Kermani), and the eleven members of the Board of Trustees. Closes with patron tiers (Iwan Patron, Tilework Circle, Atelier Friend) and a contact for bequests.
